subject: Zenit APAC migration - temporary p95 adjustment request
messages:
From: Raj Patel <raj.patel@zenithealth.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: APAC migration - temporary SLO ask

Hi Priya,

Quick context: our platform team at Zenit is switching the primary traffic ingress for a subset of users to APAC on May 25 for a 72-hour migration window. We anticipate an elevated tail (spiky bursts) during cutover while routing and CDN caches warm up.

Can Redwood temporarily relax the p95 latency commitment for Hosted API in the APAC region for the migration window? Specifically we're asking to move p95 from 300ms -> 600ms for the 72-hour period (May 25 00:00 UTC - May 27 23:59 UTC). We understand this is an exception; we have a mutual action plan (attached traffic profile + migration steps) and will run a synthetic tester and cooperate on tracing.

Requirements from our side:
- We will pin traffic to an APAC region flag for the migration cohort.
- We'll provide a cadence of hourly traffic samples.
- We need a written addendum to the SLO for procurement.

Please let me know if this is feasible and what the internal approvals would be. We prefer the shortest, well-scoped carveout rather than moving our SLA baseline.

Thanks,
Raj
Raj Patel
Head of Cloud Operations, Zenit Health

Team — forwarding Zenit’s request. TL;DR: customer asks for a regional p95 relaxation to 600ms for a 72-hour window (May 25–27) to cover cutover. They’ll provide traffic samples and agree to synthetic checks.

What I need:
- Operational guardrails we require from SRE (Karthik) — e.g., one-way ramp, prefix caching, throttles, explicit tracing tag.
- CS communications plan and synthetic checklist (Marissa).
- Legal/procurement note: this must be an addendum with explicit start/end UTC times and a clause that the exception is not precedent. Naomi — will procurement require any change to revenue recognition or billing?

I propose we keep the exception scoped to: APAC region only, cohort pinned by header flag, p95 -> 600ms, one-time 72-hour window, no changes to billing. If SRE requires it, we can do a staged ramp (12h ramp, 48h steady, 12h ramp down).

Please reply with approvals or blockers by EOD tomorrow so I can confirm to Raj.

Priya — I’m okay with granting a scoped exception provided we operationalize monitoring and clear rollback triggers. My asks:
- Require Zenit to run a production-like synthetic at 5m cadence for the entire window and share results.
- We publish a temporary dashboard (shared link) showing p50/p95 and error/allocation per minute.
- Set rollback triggers: sustained p95 > 900ms for >30m OR >2% errors for >15m -> automatic throttle to reduced traffic cohort.

Communication plan: send one pre-cutover notice and hourly updates during the first 12 hours, then 4-hour cadence. Marissa will own the communications and escalation with the customer.

Approve from CS side for the proposed 72-hour window and the staged ramp.

-Marissa

Team — SRE notes and conditions:
- We can accept a temporary p95 of 600ms for APAC if the following are implemented before start time:
  * Regional prefix caching enabled and verified with a warm-up plan.
  * A header-based cohort flag so we can limit scope to their cohort.
  * Synthetic tests and traces forwarded to our tracing project with the header tag.
  * Real-time log export to the incident buffer for the window.
- Operational limits: apply a hard concurrency cap per org to prevent noisy neighbor impact.
- Observability: we need the temporary dashboard and a live pager rotation for the first 24 hours.
- Billing: exceptional SLO adjustments must not change billing or SL credits; legal can specify but ops will not modify usage meters.

If those conditions are met, SRE approves the carveout. I’ll schedule a 30-min runbook walk-through with Zenit and Marissa tomorrow.

-Karthik

Hi Raj — thanks for the quick responses and for providing the traffic file. Per our internal review we can grant a one-time, region-scoped SLO carveout subject to the conditions below. Please review and confirm so we can produce a signed addendum.

Approved carveout (summary):
- Scope: APAC region only, requests must present header flag X-Zenit-Migration: true (or equivalent).
- Window: 2026-05-25T00:00:00Z through 2026-05-27T23:59:59Z (UTC).
- Latency target during window: p50 unchanged; p95 target relaxed from 300ms -> 600ms.
- Billing: no change to billing or SLO credits — this is an operational exception only.
- Operational conditions:
  * Zenit to run a synthetic at 5-minute cadence for the cohort and forward traces to Redwood tracing project "zenit-migration".
  * Regional prefix caching must be enabled and warmed prior to start.
  * Hard org-level concurrency caps applied by Redwood for the cohort.
  * Temporary dashboard and pager rotation for first 24 hours; rollback triggers as discussed.

Deliverables before start: signed addendum (we will send an editable PDF), completed runbook walkthrough with Karthik and Marissa, and confirmation of synthetic test results.

If you confirm, we’ll issue the addendum and schedule the runbook call (30 min) at your earliest availability. We’ll also provide an hourly update cadence during the initial 12 hours and a 4-hour cadence thereafter.

Thanks — looking forward to the sync.

Best,
